query_text: Someone intercepted my net banking OTP and used my electronic signature without permission to transfer funds.
rationale: Fraudulent use of electronic signature, OTP, and authentication credentials constitutes identity theft under Section 66C IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Clear digital credential misuse without consent.

query_text: A scammer created a fake Facebook account with my name and photos and messaged my friends asking for money pretending to be in an emergency.
rationale: Impersonation using computer resources / social media to deceive constitutes cheating by personation under Section 66D IT Act and Section 319 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Both cyber and general criminal impersonation apply.

query_text: An individual induced me to pay fifty thousand rupees for a government job offer that turned out to be completely fabricated.
rationale: Deceptive inducement to deliver money causing financial loss constitutes cheating under Section 318 BNS.
reviewer_notes: General financial fraud with delivery of property.

query_text: A hidden camera was placed in a hotel changing room capturing private intimate images of guests without their knowledge or consent.
rationale: Capturing images of private body parts under circumstances violating privacy without consent constitutes Section 66E IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Direct privacy violation under statutory definition.

query_text: The suspect uploaded sexually explicit videos depicting non-consensual sexual acts onto public telegram channels.
rationale: Electronic transmission of material containing sexually explicit acts is penalised under Section 67A IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Distinguished from simple obscenity due to explicit act depiction.

query_text: A man followed me from my workplace daily and kept messaging me despite my repeated written instructions to stay away.
rationale: Following a woman and attempting contact repeatedly despite clear indication of disinterest constitutes stalking under Section 78 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Classic physical stalking provision.

query_text: The caller threatened to kill my children and burn down my shop unless I dropped my civil suit against his brother.
rationale: Threatening injury to person or property to cause alarm or compel an act constitutes criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Aggravated threat of death/destruction.

query_text: A blackmailer threatened to disseminate private financial documents to the media unless our firm paid ten lakh rupees by Friday.
rationale: Putting in fear of injury/reputational harm to induce delivery of money constitutes extortion (Section 308 BNS) and intimidation (Section 351 BNS).
reviewer_notes: Dual offense of extortion and criminal intimidation.

query_text: A rogue contractor logged into our production server without credentials and downloaded our confidential client database.
rationale: Unauthorized access and downloading of computer data without owner permission violates Section 43 (civil) and Section 66 (criminal) IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Both civil damage under 43 and criminal hacking under 66 apply.

query_text: A shopkeeper bought stolen laptops from a burglar knowing they were taken from an IT firm office.
rationale: Dishonestly receiving or retaining stolen computer resources with knowledge or belief constitutes Section 66B IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Knowledge of stolen nature is present in facts.

query_text: A former colleague published false allegations on LinkedIn claiming I committed embezzlement, damaging my career prospects.
rationale: Publishing false defamatory imputations online intending or knowing it will harm reputation constitutes defamation under Section 356 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Defamation via electronic professional platform.

query_text: An intruder sneaked into our home and stole gold jewelry and cash from the bedroom safe while we were asleep.
rationale: Dishonestly taking movable property out of possession without consent is theft under Section 303 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Physical theft of movable property.

query_text: The tenant defaulted on monthly rent payments for three months and refused to vacate upon lease expiry.
rationale: Breach of tenancy lease agreement is a civil property dispute outside the indexed criminal/cyber statutory provisions.
reviewer_notes: Civil tenancy matter: expected no-match in criminal corpus.

query_text: The airline cancelled my flight without prior notice and customer service refused to process a refund.
rationale: Consumer dispute regarding service deficiency is outside the indexed criminal/cyber statutory provisions.
reviewer_notes: Consumer protection / civil forum matter.

query_text: The driver received a traffic challan for speeding and running a red light on the ring road.
rationale: Motor Vehicles Act offenses are not included in the indexed criminal and cyber provisions.
reviewer_notes: Motor Vehicles Act out of scope.

query_text: An unauthorized party created a clone of my Aadhaar card details and registered a SIM card under my identity.
rationale: Misuse of unique identification features (Aadhaar) constitutes identity theft under Section 66C IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Aadhaar qualifies as unique identification feature.

query_text: A cyber attacker sent an email posing as the company CFO instructing the finance desk to transfer funds to an offshore bank account.
rationale: Business Email Compromise (BEC) posing as another officer using computer resources is cheating by personation under 66D IT Act and 319 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Corporate impersonation fraud.

query_text: A man continually tracked a woman's movements using spyware installed on her mobile phone and monitored her incoming emails.
rationale: Monitoring a woman's use of the internet, email, or electronic communication constitutes cyber-stalking under Section 78 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Electronic monitoring subsection of stalking statute.

query_text: A competitor circulated vulgar and sexually obscene cartoons depicting our staff members on WhatsApp groups.
rationale: Transmitting obscene material in electronic form is punishable under Section 67 IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Obscene digital media circulation.

query_text: A malware payload was transmitted into our banking server, which encrypted database files and disrupted branch transactions.
rationale: Introducing computer contaminant/virus and disrupting computer systems violates Section 43 and Section 66 IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Ransomware / computer contaminant disruption.

query_text: A stranger threatened to beat me up and break my legs if I testified in court next Monday.
rationale: Threatening injury to person to deter an act (testifying) constitutes criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Direct threat to person.

query_text: In March 2024, a salesman tricked me into handing over my property deed by falsely promising lucrative joint venture returns.
rationale: Offense committed prior to 1 July 2024 involving dishonest inducement to deliver property falls under historical Section 420 IPC.
reviewer_notes: Temporal applicability: Pre-July 2024 criminal act governed by IPC.

query_text: In January 2024, a criminal impersonated an income tax inspector to demand cash bribes from shopkeepers.
rationale: Historical cheating by personation committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 419 IPC.
reviewer_notes: Pre-July 2024 impersonation.

query_text: The city municipal corporation issued a property tax assessment notice with an unexpected surcharge.
rationale: Municipal tax assessments are administrative revenue matters outside criminal/cyber penal provisions.
reviewer_notes: Tax revenue assessment out of scope.

query_text: A neighbor complained about loud construction music playing at 3 PM during permitted renovation hours.
rationale: Permitted daytime renovation noise is a local nuisance/civil matter not covered by indexed penal provisions.
reviewer_notes: Local municipal nuisance out of scope.

query_text: Someone logged into my work email account using stolen credentials and sent offensive emails to our leadership team.
rationale: Use of stolen login credentials (66C) and unauthorized computer access/tampering (66) IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Needs confirmation on whether 66 alone or 66C+66 is the primary expectation.

query_text: A vendor manufactured counterfeit branded handbags mimicking our registered trademark logo.
rationale: Trademark infringement under Trade Marks Act, 1999 is outside indexed penal and cyber provisions.
reviewer_notes: Intellectual property infringement out of scope; verify if cheating (318 BNS) could arguably apply.

query_text: The blackmailer told me he would post private photographs of my family unless I withdrew my police complaint.
rationale: Threat to reputation to coerce omission of legal right (withdrawing complaint) constitutes criminal intimidation under 351 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Check if extortion (308 BNS) is triggered in absence of property demand.

query_text: A person recorded a conversation in a restaurant without informing the other attendees.
rationale: Recording audio in a public restaurant where no reasonable expectation of bodily privacy exists does not constitute Section 66E IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Likely out of scope; pending review of admissibility vs statutory offense.

query_text: Someone placed a GPS magnetic tracker under my vehicle and monitored everywhere I drove for two weeks.
rationale: Electronic tracking of a woman's movements constitutes stalking under Section 78 BNS if targeted person is female.
reviewer_notes: Factual query lacks explicit gender specification; pending annotator review.

query_text: An impostor accessed my corporate email account by resetting my security questions and used my identity to authorize wire payments.
rationale: Fraudulent use of authentication credentials (66C) and cheating by personation through computer resources (66D).
reviewer_notes: Corporate identity takeover and fraud.

query_text: A fraudster created a fake profile pretending to be a bank compliance officer and extracted customer account details.
rationale: Digital personation to cheat customers constitutes 66D IT Act and 319 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Phishing personation scam.

query_text: A fraudulent financial scheme promised double returns in one month and ran away with three crore rupees of investor savings.
rationale: Deceptive inducement to deliver property resulting in heavy loss constitutes cheating under 318 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Ponzi scheme style cheating.

query_text: Intimate photographs of a person were secretly captured through a peephole in a fitting room and shared on adult forums.
rationale: Capturing and transmitting intimate private area images without consent under reasonable privacy expectations constitutes 66E IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Voyeurism and transmission under IT Act 66E.

query_text: Pornographic video clips featuring explicit sexual acts were uploaded to a public community website.
rationale: Transmitting sexually explicit acts electronically is penalized under Section 67A IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Explicit digital media dissemination.

query_text: A rejected suitor persistently stalked a college student, following her to classes and calling her incessantly despite her protests.
rationale: Following a woman and attempting repeated contact despite clear disinterest constitutes Section 78 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Classic physical stalking scenario.

query_text: The gang leader threatened to burn our factory and shoot our guards unless we stopped manufacturing goods in that territory.
rationale: Threatening injury to property and person to coerce omission of legal trade rights constitutes criminal intimidation under 351 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Intimidation targeting property and physical safety.

query_text: Cyber criminals locked our hospital databases with ransomware and demanded 10 bitcoins to restore patient files.
rationale: Extortion via digital ransom demand (308 BNS) combined with criminal damage to computer systems (66 IT Act).
reviewer_notes: Ransomware extortion and system disruption.

query_text: An external hacker executed unauthorized scripts to bypass authentication and dump user password hashes from our cloud servers.
rationale: Unauthorized access and copying of data without owner permission under Sections 43 and 66 IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Server breach and credential dumping.

query_text: A pawn shop owner acquired twenty smartphones knowing they were stolen from an electronics warehouse.
rationale: Dishonestly receiving stolen communication devices with knowledge constitutes 66B IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Stolen mobile devices.

query_text: A local politician posted fabricated claims on Twitter asserting our hospital doctors intentionally poisoned patients.
rationale: Publishing false defamatory imputations to harm medical reputation constitutes Section 356 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Public online defamation.

query_text: A delivery boy snatched a customer's diamond necklace and fled on a motorbike.
rationale: Dishonestly moving movable property out of possession without consent constitutes theft under 303 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Physical theft of movable valuables.

query_text: The e-commerce seller delivered shoes of size 8 instead of size 9 and refused to accept return for exchange.
rationale: Consumer product return dispute without fraudulent inducement at inception is a civil consumer grievance.
reviewer_notes: Civil consumer forum matter.

query_text: The bank charged a quarterly minimum balance maintenance fee on my savings account.
rationale: Contractual banking fee imposition is a civil commercial matter outside penal law.
reviewer_notes: Banking contract charge.

query_text: A restaurant served soup that was slightly cold and took twenty minutes to bring the bill.
rationale: Service dissatisfaction in a dining establishment is outside legal offense categories.
reviewer_notes: Trivial consumer service dissatisfaction.

query_text: An unauthorized party guessed my Wi-Fi router password and used my home broadband connection for three days.
rationale: Securing unauthorized access to a computer network without permission of the owner under Section 43 IT Act.
reviewer_notes: Needs annotator review on whether Section 66 is also satisfied without demonstrable damage.

query_text: In December 2023, an accountant embezzled funds by submitting forged invoices to the finance department.
rationale: Historical cheating committed before 1 July 2024 governed by Section 420 IPC.
reviewer_notes: Pre-BNS fraudulent inducement; check if forgery provisions outside corpus are needed.

query_text: Someone took pictures of our company storefront from a public street sidewalk during business hours.
rationale: Taking photographs of a public storefront does not violate privacy or criminal provisions.
reviewer_notes: No reasonable expectation of privacy for public storefront.

query_text: A user created a parody account on social media clearly labeled as satire of a celebrity.
rationale: Explicit parody/satire lacking deceptive fraudulent inducement is not criminal personation.
reviewer_notes: Parody exception under IT Act / absence of deceptive intent.

query_text: A man sent fifty unsolicited romantic poems to a coworker's official email despite her repeated requests to stop.
rationale: Repeated unwanted electronic communication to a woman despite clear disinterest constitutes Section 78 BNS.
reviewer_notes: Electronic harassment / stalking.
